examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions Involving Tautologies and Contradictions
examples.worked_solution:
Let's simplify the expression using the properties of logical operation

- First, we use that $X \Rightarrow Y  \equiv \neg X \lor Y {:}$

$$
(A \land \neg B)\Rightarrow \neg B \equiv
	\neg (A \land \neg B) \lor \neg B
$$

- Next, we use a De Morgan's law:

$$
{\color{blue}\neg (A \land \neg B)} \lor \neg B \equiv
	{\color{blue}(\neg A \lor \neg  \neg B)} \lor \neg B
$$

- Then,  we simplify the double negation:

$$
(\neg A \lor {\color{blue}\neg \neg} B) \lor \neg B  \equiv
	(\neg A \lor B) \lor \neg B
$$

- Next, we use the associative law:

$$
(\neg A \lor B) \lor \neg B  \equiv 
	\neg A \lor (B \lor \neg B)
$$

- Then,  we use the fact that the disjunction of an expression and its negation is a tautology:

$$
\neg A \lor  {\color{blue} (B \lor \neg B)}   \equiv
	\neg A \lor {\color{blue} \textrm{t}}
$$

- Finally, we use the fact that the disjunction of an expression and a tautology gives  a tautology:

$$
\neg A \lor  \textrm{t}  \equiv   \textrm{t}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
(A \land \neg B) \Rightarrow \neg B  \equiv   \textrm{t}
$$

feedback.problem:
If $P$ is a statement, $\text{t}$ is a tautology, and $\text{c}$ is a contradiction, complete the following table of logical equivalences.

| Statement | Is Logically Equivalent To |
| --- | --- |
| $\text{c}∧\text{t}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{c}∨\text{c}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $¬P∨\text{c}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $¬P∨\text{t}$ | {{field-4}} |
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall the following properties of tautologies and contradictions:

$$
\begin{aligned}A∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & A∧\text{t} & =A \\ A∨\text{c}=A\, &  & A∧\text{c} & =\text{c} \\ \text{t}∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{t}∧\text{t} & =\text{t} \\ \text{t}∨\text{c}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{t}∧\text{c} & =\text{c} \\ \text{c}∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{c}∧\text{t} & =\text{c} \\ \text{c}∨\text{c}=\text{c}\, &  & \text{c}∧\text{c} & =\text{c}\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is shown below.

| Statement | Is Logically Equivalent To |
| --- | --- |
| $\text{c}∧\text{t}$ | $\text{c}$ |
| $\text{c}∨\text{c}$ | $\text{c}$ |
| $¬P∨\text{c}$ | $¬P$ |
| $¬P∨\text{t}$ | $\text{t}$ |
